turn_text: Senator, it's one thing to sign a trade agreement and it's another to keep the players honest to living up to what they have said that they would do. The question at point here is Mexico and now they're banned of genetically enhanced crops. How do you evaluate how the USS handled the situation so far and how important to keep both Canada and Mexico's feet to the fire with what they've promised to do?

Well obviously we need to honor trade agreements and for darn sure Mexico needs to honor trade agreements as well. You know for them to double down on their efforts now to ban our our exports, their imports of GMO corn by 2024. That is outrageous. We have a trade agreement. It is based on science. There shouldn't be any flexibility here. It's a violation of the USMCA. It's not based in science. I was pleased that Canada joined us. in asking for some technical consultations. Again, this will be step by step so that we can pursue a dispute settlement with them. I've been working with the U.S. Trade Representative, Ambassador Ty about this, spoken with her directly a number of times. I organized a letter with a bipartisan group of 25 senators to encourage the ambassador and also Secretary Vilsack to hold Mexico to its trade commitments. And I would say to you, I have been pleased up to this point that they have stepped forward. They've been, I think, very strong in dealing with Mexico, and I would hope they continue to be because this doesn't just affect corn and white corn going to Mexico. If you have a trade partner say to you that GMOs aren't safe, that's just ludicrous that they would say that. There's no basis for that at all.
